subject: science
intro: Natural selection is the process by which organisms with traits better suited to their environment tend to survive and reproduce more than others. Within a population there is genetic variation, so individuals differ. When a trait gives an individual a better chance of surviving and reproducing in a specific environment, that individual passes the trait to more offspring. Over generations, the helpful trait becomes more common in the population.

items.prompt: In a population of beetles on dark tree bark, some beetles are dark and some are light. Birds eat beetles they can see easily. Which beetles are more likely to survive and reproduce?

steps: On dark bark, dark beetles are harder for birds to see.
Harder-to-see beetles are eaten less, so they survive and reproduce more.
So the dark beetles are more likely to survive and reproduce.
solution.answer: The dark beetles, because they are better camouflaged on dark bark.

items.prompt: After many generations on dark bark, what happens to the fraction of dark beetles, and why?

steps: Dark beetles survive and reproduce more, passing on the dark-color trait.
Each generation has more dark beetles than before.
So the fraction of dark beetles increases over time.
solution.answer: The fraction of dark beetles increases, because they reproduce more and pass on the trait.

items.prompt: Why is genetic variation necessary for natural selection to occur?

steps: Natural selection acts on differences among individuals.
Without variation, all individuals would be the same and none would have an advantage.
So variation is needed for selection to favor some traits.
solution.answer: Because selection needs differences; without variation there is no advantage to select.

items.prompt: What must a population have for natural selection to act on it?

steps: A population must have genetic variation for natural selection to act.

items.prompt: What happens to a helpful trait over many generations?

steps: A helpful trait becomes more common over generations.
